turns.doctor_question: Hello, I’m Dr. ___. What brings you in today?
turns.patient_response:
Um... I was told to come in. It's... well, it's about work. Dispatch and compliance, they've been tracking my route changes. Through the computer system. And... there are these little comments on the radio. 

Everyone keeps saying it’s just normal oversight, but... I can just tell certain drivers are reporting on me. That's all.

symptom_reasoning.S019: The patient expresses a fixed belief that dispatch and coworkers are tracking and reporting on them despite evidence to the contrary, indicating persecutory delusions.

turns.doctor_question: How long have you been noticing these concerns?
turns.patient_response: Um... maybe about eight months? It... it started around the time they made me the temporary dispatch lead at work. I guess it's just been building up since then.

turns.doctor_question: Before this started, would you say you’ve generally been a very suspicious or mistrustful person for most of your adult life?
turns.patient_response: No. Um... I don't think so. I usually just... keep to myself, mostly. I didn't really have a reason to not trust people before.

turns.doctor_question: Have you noticed any changes in your thinking or behavior that other people have pointed out as odd or unusual?
turns.patient_response: Um... I guess at work, sometimes. People look at me like... like I'm being difficult. But I'm not. I just... I get stuck sometimes, rearranging the magnets and the route slips. They need to be in a certain pattern. Or I might repeat a driver's last few words back before I answer them. They think it's weird, but... I'm really just trying to keep the whole board from going wrong.

symptom_reasoning.S022: The patient describes repeating the last few words spoken by others (echolalia) and engaging in odd, repetitive behaviors at work.
symptom_reasoning.S066: The patient describes a strong urge to rearrange items in a specific pattern to prevent a negative outcome ('keep the whole board from going wrong'), indicative of ordering and arranging compulsions.

turns.doctor_question: Do other people ever have trouble following the way you speak?
turns.patient_response: Um... I don't think so. I don't really talk to people that much anyway. Just... what I need to for work. So, no, they haven't said anything.

symptom_reasoning.S023: The patient states they do not talk to people much, indicating asociality or diminished social interest.
symptom_reasoning.S021: The patient explicitly denies that others have trouble following their speech.

turns.doctor_question: Have you noticed a drop in your work performance or ability to keep up with everyday responsibilities since this started?
turns.patient_response: Um... yeah, I guess. At work, I'm... I'm behind on the route reports. And some of the drivers have been complaining that my instructions are confusing. I don't know. And at home... my husband is doing mostly everything now. The meals, making calls... all the planning. I just... I haven't been keeping up with it.

symptom_reasoning.S004: The patient reports failing to finish workplace duties (falling behind on route reports) and household chores (husband taking over meals and calls because she cannot keep up).
symptom_reasoning.S005: The patient notes that her husband has had to take over 'all the planning' at home, indicating difficulty organizing tasks and activities.

turns.doctor_question: Do you believe the radio comments and route tracking are definitely being directed at you by other people?
turns.patient_response: Um... yes. I mean, dispatch and compliance... they track my route changes through the computer system. And those little comments on the radio. People try to tell me it's just normal oversight, but... it's not. I can just tell that certain drivers are reporting on me.

symptom_reasoning.S019: The patient confirms a fixed belief that they are being tracked and reported on by dispatch and other drivers, despite others telling them it is just normal oversight, indicating persecutory/referential delusions.

turns.doctor_question: Have you ever felt that your thoughts were being inserted into your mind, taken out of your mind, or broadcast so other people could hear them?

symptom_reasoning.S019: The patient explicitly denies experiencing thought insertion, withdrawal, or broadcasting, which are types of delusions.

turns.doctor_question: Have you become more socially withdrawn or less interested in things you used to enjoy?
turns.patient_response: Yeah... I suppose so. I just... I don't really feel like singing with the choir anymore. Or having the softball team over. I just stay in. Most days after my shift, I just sit at the kitchen table. I'll have the planner open, but... I don't know, I just can't make myself start dinner, or make calls, or... anything, really. I just sit there.

symptom_reasoning.S025: The patient confirms social withdrawal and a loss of interest in previously enjoyed activities, such as singing with the choir and hosting the softball team.

turns.doctor_question: Before these past eight months, had you generally been suspicious of other people or felt that they might be talking about you for most of your adult life?
turns.patient_response: Um... no. Not really. I usually just... keep to myself, so I don't think I paid much attention to what other people were doing back then.

turns.doctor_question: Have you ever had periods in the past when you believed others were trying to harm or watch you, before the last eight months?
turns.patient_response: No... I haven't. Nothing like that before.

turns.doctor_question: Have you had any hallucinations, like seeing things that aren’t there?

turns.doctor_question: Do you think there’s any chance that your concerns about the radio comments and route tracking could be mistaken?
turns.patient_response: No... I don't think so. I know people keep saying it’s just... normal oversight. But I can tell.
